docs.title: What is LACCP?
docs.text:
The Local Area Common Clock Protocol (LACCP) synchronizes timestamps across FPGA-based electronics. It is an upper-layer protocol of the MIKUMARI link protocol and is intended for systems such as distributed data acquisition (DAQ), where measurements from different nodes must share a time reference.

LACCP provides heartbeat-counter synchronization, heartbeat-frame information, and a fine timing correction. The acquisition logic combines this information with its measurements to produce timestamps relative to the reference node.

This page introduces the concepts. See LACCP for the RTL architecture and interfaces, or Usage to integrate the blocks into a design.

docs.title: Relationship with MIKUMARI
docs.text:
MIKUMARI carries a clock signal and data over the same physical link using clock duty-cycle modulation. The receiving node recovers its clocks from the modulated signal. LACCP uses the communication services of this link to establish a common time reference.

Layer Responsibility User acquisition logic Capture measurements and apply the fine correction to their timestamps. LACCP Synchronize heartbeat counters and frame information; calculate the fine offset. MIKUMARI Provide clock-frequency synchronization, data-frame communication, and fixed-latency pulse transmission.

Frequency synchronization alone does not align timestamps: the recovered clock has a phase offset, and the link introduces propagation delay. LACCP accounts for these effects through counter synchronization and timestamp correction. It does not adjust the recovered clock phase to match the reference clock.

Physical connections, clock generation and recovery, and FPGA I/O constraints are described in the MIKUMARI User Guide.

docs.title: Primary and secondary
docs.text:
The roles are defined for each link:

Role Meaning Primary Supplies the reference clock and time information to the other endpoint. Secondary Recovers the clock and synchronizes its time information to the primary.

In a tree-shaped network, the root supplies the original time reference. A relay node acts as a secondary toward its upstream neighbor and as a primary toward downstream neighbors. These roles describe a connection, rather than a permanent classification of an entire FPGA.

docs.title: Timestamps and heartbeat frames
docs.text:
Each node maintains a heartbeat counter driven by its local system clock. A heartbeat marks the counter rollover, and the interval between heartbeats is called a heartbeat frame. A frame number distinguishes successive frames.

Time information Purpose Heartbeat counter Identify a system-clock interval within a heartbeat frame. Heartbeat frame number Identify the frame containing that interval. Fine offset Correct the residual timing difference between the local and reference time bases.

The counter and frame number provide the coarse timestamp. The fine offset is a signed correction used by the acquisition logic; it is not an additional counter. The resolution of a measurement within a clock interval depends on the acquisition circuit, such as a TDC, rather than on LACCP alone.

LACCP also distributes heartbeat-frame state and flags. These allow acquisition logic to associate activity and status information with the shared frame structure. Timing pulses can carry trigger or reset indications whose effects are implemented by the receiving application.

docs.title: How synchronization works
docs.text:
1. MIKUMARI establishes communication between the primary and secondary.
  2. LACCP measures a pulse round-trip time and exchanges receiver-delay information.
  3. The secondary calculates its counter offset and fine offset, then synchronizes its heartbeat counter and frame information.
  4. After the completion exchange, the endpoints report readiness for acquisition.

This is a conceptual sequence: delay-information exchanges and pulse measurements can overlap. Synchronization is performed during initialization; the fine correction is then used by the acquisition logic.

Figure 1

The figure shows the timing relationship after coarse synchronization. Both counters identify corresponding clock intervals, but their rollover edges remain separated because the reference and recovered clocks have different phases. In the illustrated case, the secondary heartbeat is earlier than the primary heartbeat, so the local fine offset is negative. The acquisition logic adds this signed correction to its local measurement timestamp; the clocks themselves remain unchanged.

The lower part shows the flow of time information. The primary Heartbeat Unit supplies heartbeat and frame information, while the secondary Heartbeat Unit synchronizes its local counter and frame number. Acquisition logic uses this coarse time information together with the fine offset from LACCP to timestamp its data. The DAQ data format and insertion of frame-number information are application functions.

This conceptual illustration follows the example on slide 9 of R. Honda, MIKUMARI, the time synchronization protocol in the SPADI Alliance (SRO XIV). It omits internal pipeline delays and implementation-specific wiring; see Heartbeat Units for the RTL output timing.

Synchronization accuracy depends on the delay estimation and the physical implementation, including differences between the two transmission directions. The results reported in the reference papers describe their evaluated configurations, rather than a guarantee for arbitrary hardware.

docs.title: From one link to a network
docs.text:
Synchronization proceeds from upstream nodes to downstream nodes. A downstream secondary combines its local fine offset with the correction supplied from upstream. This gives its timestamp a reference to the root, rather than only to its immediate neighbor.

The clock-distribution topology and the propagation of time information must be designed together. The RTL interfaces for accumulated offsets and interconnects are described in LACCP; their connections are covered in Usage.

docs.title: LACCP
docs.text: This page describes the architecture, behavior, and public interfaces of the current LACCP RTL. Signal names follow the source, including spellings such as serdesLantencyIn. For wiring and initialization, see Usage.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Figure 1

LaccpMainBlock implements the LACCP endpoint attached to one MIKUMARI link. It contains the following blocks.

Block Function LaccpFrameRx Parse the nine-byte LACCP frame received through MIKUMARI. LaccpFrameTx Serialize a LACCP frame body into a MIKUMARI normal frame. LaccpBusSwitch Distribute frame bodies among the MIKUMARI port, local protocol blocks, and interconnect ports. RCAP Measure round-trip time, exchange timing parameters, and calculate synchronization offsets. RLIGP Exchange application-supplied link information with the other endpoint.

The Heartbeat Unit and MIKUMARI blocks are external to LaccpMainBlock. PrimaryHeartBeatUnit generates the root heartbeat and frame information. HeartBeatUnit receives this information and synchronizes a secondary, or operates independently in stand-alone mode.

The frame path is MIKUMARI <-> FrameRx/FrameTx <-> BusSwitch <-> protocol blocks. The pulse path connects directly to the synchronization and user-pulse logic; pulses are not encoded as LACCP frame bodies. The diagram groups the HBU synchronization interfaces with RCAP; their public ports are on LaccpMainBlock, which routes the heartbeat pulses.

docs.title: Frame format
docs.text:
defLaccp.vhd defines a nine-byte frame. LaccpFrameTx sends the preamble first, followed by the frame body from its most significant byte to its least significant byte.

Byte Field Frame-body bits 0 Preamble, 0xFA Not included in the bus frame body. 1 Destination module address and local address 63:60 and 59:56 2 Source module address and local address 55:52 and 51:48 3 Command bits 47:40 4 Reserved 39:32 5–8 Register value, most significant byte first 31:0

LaccpFrameBobyType is the 64-bit frame-body type. The module address selects a protocol endpoint, such as RCAP; the local address selects an operation within that endpoint. These fields are separate from the 32-bit link information exchanged by RLIGP.

Command bit RTL constant Meaning 0 kCmdPassagePermission Permit forwarding to interconnect ports. 1 kCmdDepature Permit transmission through the local MIKUMARI port. 2 kCmdWrite Write operation. 3 kCmdRead Read-operation bit defined in the package. 4 kCmdReply Reply operation. 5 kCmdReplyRequest Request a reply.

The presence of a command constant does not imply that every endpoint implements that operation. The supplied RCAP, RLIGP, and Heartbeat Unit receive logic handles its specific write and reply operations.

The receiver checks the preamble, expected body length, final-byte indication, and checksum status at the expected final byte before releasing a frame body. frameBrokenRx and recvTermndRx are inputs to the receiver, but the current parser does not use them to change its receive state.

docs.title: Bus ports and forwarding
docs.text:
Internal port Destination module address Endpoint 0 Not a local protocol address MIKUMARI frame transport 1 0x1 RLIGP 2 0x2 RCAP 3 0x3 External Heartbeat Unit 4 onward Selected by forwarding rules Interconnects

Destination module address 0x0 broadcasts to the local protocol ports. A frame is not returned to its originating local port for an ordinary addressed transfer. Passage permission forwards frames to the configured interconnects only when the ingress is not itself an interconnect. Departure permits transmission through MIKUMARI only when the ingress is not MIKUMARI. Interconnect forwarding is a fan-out operation, not an address-to-link routing table.

The current package exposes one external intra port, at array index 0, for the Heartbeat Unit. The external interconnect arrays have 32 elements; kNumInterconnect selects the implemented prefix. With no interconnects, use kNumInterconnect = 0. Do not consume output elements outside the configured prefix: the main block does not drive them.

Bus data is a complete 64-bit frame body. Assert the associated input-valid signal for one clock to enqueue one body. Receiver readiness gates the output-valid pulse during forwarding; it is not a per-frame acknowledgment or a mechanism that holds a transfer until the destination becomes ready. The switch and protocol FIFOs have finite capacity and do not expose upstream flow control through these ports. Keep custom traffic within the receiver's processing capacity.

docs.title: RCAP
docs.text:
RCAP stands for Remote Clock Adjustment Protocol. It has different responsibilities at the two endpoints.

Primary Secondary Return a received probe pulse. Send a probe and measure its round-trip time in system-clock counts. Send local receiver parameters, calibration data, and upstreamOffset. Use local and received parameters to calculate the fine offset. Supply heartbeat pulses during synchronization. Apply the calculated counter offset through the external Heartbeat Unit. Receive the secondary's completion message and reply. Wait for Heartbeat Unit synchronization, send the completion message, and wait for its reply.

The secondary starts from half the measured round-trip count. If that count is odd, the fine correction includes half a system-clock period. RCAP combines this with the receiver-delay difference, optional calibration correction, and upstream fine offset. It adjusts the coarse counter offset when normalizing the accumulated fine offset across a system-clock boundary.

The secondary control states are Init, AdjustClock, Finalize, and Done. AdjustClock waits for hbuIsSyncedIn; Finalize waits for the completion reply. isReadyForDaq is directly connected to RCAP's completion output. The primary reports completion after receiving the secondary's completion message, so the endpoints need not assert readiness on the same clock.

docs.title: Time units and offsets
docs.text:
The arithmetic represents 1 ns as 1024 counts. One fine-offset count is therefore 1/1024 ns, approximately 0.9765625 ps. This numerical unit is not a claim about synchronization accuracy.

GetFastClockPeriod(kFastClkFreq) returns the half-period of the fast clock in these units, rounded to an integer. The current RCAP arithmetic uses eight such half-periods as a system-clock period (kFullCycle = 8). The CDCM-8 example in Usage uses a fast-clock frequency four times the system-clock frequency.

Value Representation and interpretation roundTripTime Unsigned 16-bit count of system clocks, measured by the secondary; zero in primary mode. hbcOffset Unsigned 16-bit heartbeat-counter initialization offset. The Heartbeat Unit loads this value plus one when accepting a synchronization pulse. fineOffsetLocal Signed 16-bit correction for the local link, including the odd-round-trip adjustment and local normalization. Defined by the secondary calculation. fineOffset Signed 16-bit correction after upstream accumulation and normalization. Zero in primary mode. upstreamOffset Signed 16-bit correction supplied by the integrating design for propagation to the downstream secondary. Zero at the root. calibDelay Signed 12-bit local calibration parameter, in the same fine-time units. Exchanged with the partner.

In secondary mode, use the offsets when validOffset = '1'. In primary mode, validOffset indicates reception of the secondary's completion information, and hbcOffset contains the offset reported by that secondary. fineOffsetLocal is not assigned by the primary generate branch; do not use it in primary mode.

Apply the signed fine correction to the local measurement timestamp in the acquisition data path. A positive correction increases the timestamp, and a negative correction decreases it. Preserve the sign and handle carry or borrow across clock and heartbeat-frame boundaries.

docs.title: Receiver parameters and calibration
docs.text:
The 7-series calculation uses the IDELAY tap count and signed SerDes latency. Its tap coefficient is 80 fine-time counts, equivalent to 78.125 ps. The UltraScale calculation additionally uses the initial master and slave IDELAY counter values. The current calculation identifies a 7-series receiver by a zero initial master counter value and an UltraScale receiver by a nonzero value.

With enCalibDelay = true, CalcCalibDelay adds both the local-minus-partner calibration parameter and a family-dependent digital-delay difference before the receiver-delay difference is divided by two. With false, this entire additional correction is zero. The generic defaults to false in LaccpMainBlock, even though the Verilog module has its own default.

Calibration values depend on the implementation. The RTL does not supply a universal set of board-specific values or a procedure to measure them. The reference papers discuss the underlying delay components.

docs.title: RCAP local addresses
docs.text: Local address Operation 0x0 Completion message carrying the secondary counter offset. 0x1 Exchange IDELAY tap count, SerDes latency, and upstream fine offset. 0x2 Exchange initial IDELAY counter values and calibration parameter.

docs.title: RLIGP
docs.text:
RLIGP stands for Remote Link Information Getter Protocol. It exchanges a 32-bit application-supplied value with the other endpoint. LACCP does not define an IP address format or assign a system-wide identity through this interface.

When validMyLink is asserted, RLIGP captures addrMyLink and sends it as a write with a reply request to local address 0x0 of the partner's RLIGP endpoint. It retries while waiting for a reply and stops after receiving the reply. To exchange a changed local value after completion, restart the protocol through reset.

Reception of the partner's write sets addrPartnerLink and validPartnerLink; reset clears the validity. This operation is independent of RCAP completion. isReadyForDaq does not include a check of validPartnerLink.

docs.title: Heartbeat Units
docs.text:
defHeartBeatUnit.vhd defines a 16-bit heartbeat counter and a 24-bit heartbeat-frame number. At 125 MHz, one frame lasts 524.288 microseconds, and the combined 40-bit coarse timestamp wraps after approximately 2.44 hours. These durations scale with the system-clock period.

PrimaryHeartBeatUnit increments the frame number at heartbeats. Halfway through a heartbeat frame, it samples the acquisition gate and flags and schedules the frame-information message. forceOn forces the local frame state active. primaryRst resets its counter and frame number and schedules a reset message only while the frame state is idle.

The counter, heartbeat strobe, and frame number are registered in separate processes. During a normal rollover, heartbeatOut is high with heartbeatCount = 0, and the frame number increments on the following clock, when the counter is 1. Account for this pipeline when assembling a measurement timestamp from the separate outputs. Reset, initial frame acquisition, and frame-number correction are separate cases.

In synchronized mode, HeartBeatUnit first loads its counter from hbcOffsetIn + 1 when both validOffsetIn and syncPulseIn are high. It then accepts valid global frame information and asserts isSynchronized. Subsequent messages update frame state and flags and compare the global frame number with the local one. hbfNumMismatch reports a mismatch; keepLocalHbfNum = '0' permits correction of the local frame number.

With enStandAlone = '1', HeartBeatUnit generates its local frame number and uses its local acquisition controls. This mode does not establish synchronization to another node; isSynchronized is not a stand-alone readiness indication.

Frame-information messages use local address 0x0 of the HBU endpoint. The register value contains frame state in bits 31:28, zeros in 27:26, flags in 25:24, and frame number in 23:0. The idle-only primary reset uses a broadcast write with local address 0xF.

docs.title: Generics
docs.text: Generic Type / default Meaning kPrimaryMode boolean, false Select primary (true) or secondary (false) RCAP behavior for this link. kNumInterconnect integer, 16 Number of implemented interconnects; use 0–32 to fit the fixed external arrays. kFastClkFreq real, 500.0 SerDes fast-clock frequency in MHz, used by timing calculations. enDebug boolean, false Enable the debug attributes controlled by this generic. enCalibDelay boolean, false Enable the additional calibration calculation in the secondary.

docs.title: System, user pulses, and RLIGP ports
docs.text:
SL below means std_logic; SLV, U, and S mean std_logic_vector, unsigned, and signed. Widths are the current package values.

Port Direction / type Meaning rst In, SL Active-high reset request; sampled by the internal reset shift register. clk In, SL Protocol clock; use the associated MIKUMARI parallel-clock domain. isReadyForDaq Out, SL RCAP completion for this endpoint. laccpPulsesIn In, SLV(8) One-clock user-pulse requests; assert at most one bit at a time after synchronization. laccpPulsesOut Out, SLV(8) Decoded received user pulses, suppressed while RCAP owns the pulse path. pulseInRejected Out, SL Indicates an input collision or multiple-bit pulse encoding; see operational behavior below. addrMyLink In, SLV(32) Application-supplied local link information. validMyLink In, SL Permit RLIGP to capture and send the local information. addrPartnerLink Out, SLV(32) Received partner information. validPartnerLink Out, SL Qualify addrPartnerLink.

docs.title: Timing and synchronization ports
docs.text:
Port Direction / type Meaning idelayTapIn In, U(5) Local MIKUMARI receiver tap count. serdesLantencyIn In, S(4) Local SerDes latency in half-fast-clock periods. cntValueInitIn In, SLV(9) Local initial master IDELAY counter value. cntValueSlaveInitIn In, SLV(9) Local initial slave IDELAY counter value. idelayTapOut Out, U(5) Partner tap count received through RCAP. serdesLantencyOut Out, S(4) Partner SerDes latency received through RCAP. cntValueInitOut Out, U(9) Partner initial master counter value. cntValueSlaveInitOut Out, U(9) Partner initial slave counter value. roundTripTime Out, SLV(16) Secondary round-trip measurement; zero in primary mode. calibDelay In, S(12) Local calibration parameter. calibDelayOut Out, S(12) Partner calibration parameter. hbuIsSyncedIn In, SL Secondary Heartbeat Unit synchronization feedback to RCAP. syncPulseIn In, SL Heartbeat source for the synchronization transmit path. syncPulseOut Out, SL Received heartbeat routed to the secondary HBU during synchronization. upstreamOffset In, S(16) Upstream accumulated correction to advertise to the downstream secondary. validOffset Out, SL Qualify secondary offsets, or indicate partner completion in primary mode. hbcOffset Out, SLV(16) Secondary counter offset, or the partner-reported offset in primary mode. fineOffset Out, S(16) Accumulated secondary fine correction; zero in primary mode. fineOffsetLocal Out, S(16) Local secondary correction; unused in primary mode.

Partner timing outputs are diagnostic copies of values received during the exchange, not local IDELAY control outputs. They have no separate output-valid port. Observe them after a completed exchange, rather than assuming they are valid at reset release.

docs.title: LACCP Bus ports
docs.text:
Directions are relative to LaccpMainBlock.

Port Direction / type Meaning isReadyIntraIn In, SLV(1) External intra endpoint ready to receive forwarded bodies. dataIntraIn In, ExtIntraType One 64-bit body from the external intra endpoint. validIntraIn In, SLV(1) Enqueue the corresponding input body. dataIntraOut Out, ExtIntraType Body forwarded to the external intra endpoint. validIntraOut Out, SLV(1) Qualify the forwarded body. isReadyInterIn In, SLV(32) Readiness of interconnect destinations. existInterOut Out, SLV(32) High for each configured interconnect; other elements are undriven. dataInterIn In, ExtInterType Array of 32 input frame bodies. validInterIn In, SLV(32) Input-valid indications for interconnect bodies. dataInterOut Out, ExtInterType Forwarded bodies on configured interconnects. validInterOut Out, SLV(32) Output-valid indications on configured interconnects.

docs.title: MIKUMARI ports
docs.text:
Port Direction / type Meaning mikuLinkUpIn In, SL MIKUMARI link status; low requests an internal LACCP reset. dataTx Out, CbtUDataType (8 bits) Transmit byte. validTx Out, SL Transmit byte valid. frameLastTx Out, SL Final byte of the transmitted LACCP frame. txAck In, SL MIKUMARI acknowledgment of the transmit byte. pulseTx Out, SL Pulse transmit request. pulseTypeTx Out, MikumariPulseType (3 bits) Encoded pulse index. busyPulseTx In, SL MIKUMARI pulse transmitter busy. dataRx In, CbtUDataType (8 bits) Received byte. validRx In, SL Received byte valid. frameLastRx In, SL Received frame's final-byte indication. checkSumErrRx In, SL Received checksum-error indication. frameBrokenRx In, SL Frame-start error indication, currently buffered but not acted on by the parser. recvTermndRx In, SL Receive-termination indication, currently buffered but not acted on by the parser. pulseRx In, SL Received pulse strobe. pulseTypeRx In, MikumariPulseType (3 bits) Received pulse index.

The normal-frame transmit path uses txAck to advance through bytes. Connect this interface directly to MIKUMARI; do not replace the acknowledgment with an assumed byte rate.

docs.title: Heartbeat Unit interfaces
docs.text:
Both entities have enDebug : boolean := false. The common ports are listed below; names and directions are relative to the Heartbeat Unit.

Port Direction / type Meaning rst In, SL Active-high reset request, sampled by a 16-stage shift register. clk In, SL Heartbeat and LACCP Bus clock. heartbeatOut Out, SL Local heartbeat associated with counter rollover. heartbeatCount Out, SLV(16) Local counter value. hbfNumber Out, SLV(24) Local heartbeat-frame number. clkDiv16 Out, SL Divide-by-16 output, realigned at heartbeat timing. hbfCtrlGateIn In, SL Acquisition gate sampled at half-frame timing; local control in primary or stand-alone mode. forceOn In, SL Force active frame state in primary or stand-alone mode. frameState Out, HbfStateType kActiveFrame or kIdleFrame. hbfFlagsIn In, SLV(2) Local flags sampled in primary or stand-alone mode. frameFlags Out, SLV(2) Flags associated with the local frame state. dataBusIn In, LaccpFrameBobyType Forwarded frame body from the main block. validBusIn In, SL Qualify the input body. dataBusOut Out, LaccpFrameBobyType Locally generated body; tied to zero in HeartBeatUnit. validBusOut Out, SL Qualify an outgoing body; tied low in HeartBeatUnit. isReadyOut Out, SL Bus receive readiness; tied high in both entities.

PrimaryHeartBeatUnit has one additional port:

Port Direction / type Meaning primaryRst In, SL Synchronous request to reset the time counters and send a reset message while idle.

HeartBeatUnit has the following additional ports:

Port Direction / type Meaning enStandAlone In, SL Select independent local operation instead of synchronized frame operation. keepLocalHbfNum In, SL Preserve the local frame number on subsequent mismatches when high. syncPulseIn In, SL Received synchronization heartbeat. hbcOffsetIn In, SLV(16) Counter offset to load on synchronization. validOffsetIn In, SL Qualify the counter offset. isSynchronized Out, SL Counter and global frame information have been acquired in synchronized mode. hbfNumMismatch Out, SL Most recently compared global and local frame numbers differ.

PrimaryHeartBeatUnit does not process dataBusIn or validBusIn. In synchronized HeartBeatUnit operation, frame state and flags come from upstream messages rather than the local acquisition-control inputs.

docs.title: Reset and link loss
docs.text:
The main block samples rst OR NOT mikuLinkUpIn through a 16-stage shift register. The Heartbeat Units similarly sample their own rst, but have no link-status input. Keep their clocks running and provide reset requests long enough to pass through the shift registers.

Link loss resets the main block's frame, bus, RCAP, and RLIGP logic after the shift-register delay. It does not directly reset the external Heartbeat Unit or qualify all user-pulse outputs. The integrating design must reset the secondary Heartbeat Unit for reacquisition and gate application use of timestamps and pulses with current link and readiness status.

RCAP releases its pulse takeover after completion. It does not continuously realign the heartbeat counter or recalculate the fine offset after completion; restart synchronization after a change requiring a new timing solution.

docs.title: User pulses
docs.text:
During synchronization, RCAP owns the pulse path. Received heartbeat and probe pulses are used internally, and laccpPulsesOut is zero. After completion, an index from 0 to 7 is converted between a one-hot LACCP vector and a MIKUMARI pulse type.

Downstream pulse index Package definition 0 kDownPulseTrigger 1 kDownPulseCntRst 2 kDownPulseSysRst 3–7 Reserved definitions

All upstream user-pulse indices are reserved in the current package. These names label pulse indications; they do not reset application logic automatically.

Use one-clock, one-hot requests only when the link and LACCP are ready. A request arriving while the MIKUMARI transmitter is busy or the main block already has a pulse registered sets pulseInRejected. Multiple active input bits also cause a rejection indication, but the current encoder still registers a pulse type; do not depend on the flag to suppress malformed requests. There is no user-pulse queue or automatic retry in this interface.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: This page describes a primary–secondary connection using one MIKUMARI link. It gives the LACCP connections and bring-up checks; clock generation, FPGA pin assignments, and board constraints belong to the integrating project. See Get Started for the concepts and LACCP for signal definitions.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Prepare a bidirectional MIKUMARI connection and the clocks and resets required by both endpoints. Consult the MIKUMARI User Guide for physical-layer integration. The LACCP README lists AMD 7-series and UltraScale support; the v2.0 change log also identifies UltraScale+. Its stated tool test environment is Vivado 2025.2 or earlier.

For the following connection example, use:

Setting Primary Secondary Clock source Local reference Clock recovered from the primary's modulated signal MIKUMARI configuration Compatible CDCM-8 settings Matching CDCM-8 settings Example parallel / fast clock 125 / 500 MHz 125 / 500 MHz MIKUMARI pulse mode kHighPrecision = false kHighPrecision = false LACCP endpoint LaccpMainBlock in primary mode LaccpMainBlock in secondary mode Heartbeat source PrimaryHeartBeatUnit HeartBeatUnit in synchronized mode

The frequencies are example values, not a timing-closure guarantee for every device. Set kFastClkFreq to the actual fast-clock frequency. The current LACCP offset arithmetic uses eight half-fast-clock periods per system-clock period, consistent with this CDCM-8 configuration.

docs.title: Add the sources
docs.text:
Obtain the LACCP and MIKUMARI repositories and add their required RTL to the Vivado project. Use a submodule or a recorded revision so that the two source versions used by the design are identifiable.

Source group Integration action MIKUMARI Add the CBT, MIKUMARI link, and Wrapper/MikumariBlock.vhd sources needed by the selected FPGA implementation. LACCP packages Add defLaccp.vhd, defHeartBeatUnit.vhd, and defBitwiseOp.vhd from laccp/. LACCP blocks Add the main block, frame TX/RX, Bus Switch, RCAP, RLIGP, and both Heartbeat Unit entities. LACCP utility Add the VHDL utility files, including MyFifoComClock and its RAM dependencies. Timing arithmetic Add CalcFineLantency_US.v and CalcCalibDelay.v. The former instantiates udiv_q_cbt_axis, supplied by MIKUMARI together with its divider core.

Assign the VHDL sources referenced as mylib.* to the mylib library. Analyze packages before their users, and RAM units before the FIFO. Let Vivado update compile order after all files are added. No LACCP source requires VHDL-2008 according to the repository README.

RCAP references the Verilog timing modules through work.CalcFineLantency_US and work.CalcCalibDelay; preserve those mixed-language bindings when setting up project libraries. Check elaboration for both modules and their divider dependencies, including when using a 7-series secondary: the secondary generate branch instantiates the UltraScale calculation modules as well.

docs.title: Configure the nodes
docs.text: Figure 1

docs.title: Endpoint settings
docs.text:
Setting or input Primary Secondary kPrimaryMode true false kNumInterconnect 0 for this example 0 for this example kFastClkFreq Actual fast-clock frequency in MHz Actual fast-clock frequency in MHz enDebug Enable if internal debug probes are needed Enable if internal debug probes are needed enCalibDelay Set explicitly; the correction is calculated in the secondary Enable when using the additional calibration correction upstreamOffset Zero at the root Zero in this example; a secondary does not advertise upstream timing to another secondary hbuIsSyncedIn Tie low; primary RCAP does not use this feedback Connect from HeartBeatUnit.isSynchronized syncPulseIn Connect from PrimaryHeartBeatUnit.heartbeatOut Tie low for this leaf-only example

Configure the secondary HBU with enStandAlone = '0' and keepLocalHbfNum = '0'. The latter permits correction if a later received frame number differs from the local number. Tie its local hbfCtrlGateIn, forceOn, and hbfFlagsIn low when using upstream acquisition controls.

On the primary HBU, drive hbfCtrlGateIn from the acquisition gate and hbfFlagsIn from the application. For an initial synchronization check, both may be zero and forceOn may be low: synchronization does not require an active acquisition frame. Keep primaryRst low except when intentionally requesting an idle-state reset.

Set a stable 32-bit addrMyLink value at each endpoint and assert validMyLink when it is available. For a bench example, distinct constants such as 0x00000001 and 0x00000002 can identify the endpoints. These are application-chosen RLIGP values, not LACCP bus destination addresses.

docs.title: Unused ports
docs.text:
With kNumInterconnect = 0, tie isReadyInterIn and validInterIn low and all elements of dataInterIn to zero. Leave existInterOut, dataInterOut, and validInterOut open. Keep laccpPulsesIn zero until testing user pulses. Unused diagnostic outputs can be left open, including primary-mode fineOffsetLocal.

Do not tie the external intra port off: it is the HBU connection required to distribute heartbeat-frame information. On the primary, the unused syncPulseOut can be left open.

docs.title: Clocks and resets
docs.text:
For each node, use the local MIKUMARI clkPar domain for LaccpMainBlock.clk and HBU clk. Supply the serial and IDELAY reference clocks required by MIKUMARI separately. These interfaces do not include clock-domain crossing between the main block and the HBU.

Provide a system reset to the primary HBU and main block. For a secondary that must reacquire synchronization after link loss, include link loss in its HBU reset request, for example:

-- Concurrent assignments in the secondary integration architecture.
-- link_up is MikumariBlock.linkUp; all consumers use clkPar.
secondary_hbu_rst <= system_rst or not link_up;

The main block already includes not mikuLinkUpIn in its own internal reset request. The HBU does not. Keep clkPar running while resetting or reacquiring the blocks, and hold system reset for at least 16 active clock edges so it reaches their internal reset shift registers. Manage MIKUMARI power-on reset and clock recovery according to the board's clock/reset design.

docs.text:
Connect these ports at both endpoints. The arrow denotes the signal direction.

For the example's low-latency pulse mode, tie MIKUMARI pulseRegTx to zero and leave pulseRegRx open. Do not drive the MIKUMARI normal-frame input or pulse input from a second user source while they are connected to LACCP.

docs.title: Receiver timing information
docs.text:
These are local receiver measurements, including on the primary. Connect the outputs directly rather than substituting fixed tap or latency values.

MIKUMARI output LACCP input Conversion tapValueOut idelayTapIn Cast std_logic_vector to unsigned. serdesOffset serdesLantencyIn Direct signed connection. cntValueOutInit cntValueInitIn Direct vector connection. cntValueOutSlaveInit cntValueSlaveInitIn Direct vector connection.

For example, if miku_tap is the signal connected to tapValueOut, use idelayTapIn => unsigned(miku_tap) in the main block's port map. The 7-series MIKUMARI implementation supplies zero initial counter values; the UltraScale implementation supplies its measured values. Preserve this distinction because RCAP uses it to select the delay calculation.

The similarly named LACCP outputs are copies of partner information. They are not inputs for changing local IDELAY settings.

docs.text: Node Source Destination Primary PrimaryHeartBeatUnit.heartbeatOut LaccpMainBlock.syncPulseIn Secondary LaccpMainBlock.syncPulseOut HeartBeatUnit.syncPulseIn Secondary LaccpMainBlock.hbcOffset HeartBeatUnit.hbcOffsetIn Secondary LaccpMainBlock.validOffset HeartBeatUnit.validOffsetIn Secondary HeartBeatUnit.isSynchronized LaccpMainBlock.hbuIsSyncedIn

docs.title: HBU bus connection
docs.text:
At both endpoints, connect the HBU to external intra array index 0. This is internal bus port kPortHBU = 3; do not use external array index 3.

The following concurrent assignments show the complete bus connection. The hbu_* signals connect to the corresponding ports of the local Heartbeat Unit, and intra_* signals connect to the main block.

intra_data_in(0)  <= hbu_data_out;   -- HBU.dataBusOut
intra_valid_in(0) <= hbu_valid_out;  -- HBU.validBusOut
intra_ready_in(0) <= hbu_ready;      -- HBU.isReadyOut

hbu_data_in  <= intra_data_out(0);   -- HBU.dataBusIn
hbu_valid_in <= intra_valid_out(0);  -- HBU.validBusIn

Use ExtIntraType for the data arrays and vectors of kNumExtIntraPort bits for their valid/ready signals. In the main block's port map, these signals correspond to dataIntraIn, validIntraIn, isReadyIntraIn, dataIntraOut, and validIntraOut, respectively. Even though the secondary HBU generates no outgoing frames, connect its bus outputs and readiness in the same way.

docs.title: Configure timing correction
docs.text:
At the root primary, set upstreamOffset to zero. Connect a stable local calibDelay at each endpoint before starting RCAP. Values use the fine-time unit defined in Time units and offsets, rather than raw picoseconds.

Enable enCalibDelay on the secondary when applying the additional calibration correction. This enables both the family-dependent digital-delay term and the local-minus-partner calibration term. It does not merely enable a user-provided constant. With it disabled, those extra terms are omitted; do not interpret that configuration as validation of timing accuracy between arbitrary devices.

Choose calibration values from the timing characterization of the actual implementation. The repository does not provide universal values for every FPGA, pin assignment, or board. A functional bring-up with zero calibration inputs and correction disabled establishes the connection and control flow, but does not establish the accuracy of the resulting timestamp correction.

Keep timing inputs stable during the exchange. Restart synchronization after changing calibration or the clock configuration.

docs.title: Startup and verification
docs.text:
Figure 2
  1. Establish the primary clock and secondary clock-recovery path. Apply the board's power-on and protocol resets with the required clocks present.
  2. Release reset according to the clock/reset design. Confirm MIKUMARI laneUp and then linkUp at both endpoints, and check its receiver error outputs.
  3. Confirm the main blocks receive mikuLinkUpIn = '1'. Allow their reset shift registers to clear. On the secondary, the link-dependent HBU reset request must also clear.
  4. Observe the secondary's roundTripTime and wait for validOffset = '1'. Its hbcOffset and fineOffset can then be consumed. Exchanges and measurements proceed in the RTL without a software start command.
  5. Confirm the secondary HBU receives syncPulseIn, hbcOffsetIn, and validOffsetIn. Confirm heartbeat-frame messages reach its bus input and isSynchronized becomes high.
  6. Confirm that isSynchronized reaches hbuIsSyncedIn. Wait for RCAP's completion exchange and for isReadyForDaq = '1' at both endpoints.
  7. Separately check validPartnerLink and the expected addrPartnerLink at both endpoints. RLIGP completion is not part of the RCAP readiness output.

Keep application data marked unsynchronized until the link, HBU synchronization, and RCAP readiness are valid for the current connection. Readiness is an initialization result, not a measurement of the achieved timing accuracy. Validate timestamp alignment on the target hardware using a common timing reference, accounting for the measurement paths.

For a reconnect, block acquisition use of the old time solution, reset the secondary HBU as described above, and repeat the checks. Ensure that both main blocks restart RCAP, either through their link-dependent resets or an explicit reset at both endpoints. An HBU-only reset after RCAP completion does not restart the main block's RCAP exchange.

docs.title: Timestamp construction
docs.text:
Capture hbfNumber and heartbeatCount consistently with the measurement. After aligning them to the same heartbeat frame, the coarse timestamp is their 40-bit concatenation, with the frame number as the most significant part. At the example's 125 MHz clock, each coarse count represents 8 ns.

Account for the HBU output pipeline at rollover: in normal operation the counter reaches 0 and asserts the heartbeat strobe before the frame number increments on the following clock. Sampling the two outputs without boundary handling can therefore associate counter value 0 with the previous frame number. Align the measurement pipeline and frame selection explicitly; see Heartbeat Units.

For an acquisition circuit that also measures a fine time within the clock interval, form the local measurement time using that circuit's convention, then add the signed fineOffset correction after converting to common units. At this example frequency, one coarse count is 8192 LACCP fine-time counts.

As an arithmetic example, a correction value of -1024 represents -1 ns, not -1024 ps. Use sufficient signed precision and propagate carry or borrow across coarse-count and frame boundaries. The acquisition-specific timestamp format and its fine-time interpolation are outside the LACCP blocks.

docs.title: Acquisition state
docs.text: Drive the root HBU's acquisition gate, and consume frameState and frameFlags at each node to associate data with the propagated frame state. Root forceOn can force its state active; normal gate and flag updates are associated with half-frame timing. Do not substitute a combinational copy of the root gate for the HBU's frame-state output.

docs.title: User pulses
docs.text:
After both endpoints complete synchronization, assert one bit of laccpPulsesIn for one local clock. For a downstream trigger indication, use index kDownPulseTrigger. Observe the corresponding bit of laccpPulsesOut at the secondary and implement the intended application action there.

Monitor busyPulseTx and pulseInRejected; requests have no queue or automatic retry. Space requests so that the MIKUMARI transmitter is available and the previous local pulse registration has cleared. Never assert multiple pulse-vector bits together. A rejection flag does not guarantee that a malformed multiple-bit request produced no transmitted pulse.

Use link and readiness status to qualify received user pulses. During synchronization the pulse path is reserved for RCAP. System-reset and counter-reset pulse names are indications only; connect their effects explicitly in the application.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Checks laneUp stays low MIKUMARI clocks, power-on reset, pin assignments, polarity, I/O standards, IDELAY setup, and receiver errors. laneUp is high but linkUp is low MIKUMARI link configuration and both communication directions. LACCP remains in reset while its link input is low. Secondary validOffset stays low Probe pulse wiring, local tap/SerDes outputs, both initial counter values, actual kFastClkFreq, and RCAP frame exchanges. Offsets are valid but HBU synchronization stays low enStandAlone = '0', HBU reset release, sync/offset connections, and heartbeat-frame delivery through external intra port 0. HBU is synchronized but RCAP readiness stays low isSynchronized feedback wiring and the completion-message/reply path. validPartnerLink stays low Local validMyLink and stable addrMyLink at both endpoints, RLIGP frame transport, and reset state. Synchronization does not recover after reconnect Secondary HBU reset on link loss, running clocks during reset, and a fresh RCAP exchange. Frame-number mismatches persist HBU bus delivery, keepLocalHbfNum, reset sequencing, and custom bus traffic exceeding FIFO capacity. Control flow completes but timestamps disagree Signed fine-offset application, its unit conversion, coarse/fine capture boundaries, calibration, and directional path asymmetry. pulseInRejected is asserted Multiple active request bits, a busy pulse transmitter, or a previous pulse still registered locally.

For internal observation, enable the relevant enDebug generics and inspect the marked signals with the project's debug setup. The public signals listed above remain the primary checks for integration.

docs.title: Extending the configuration
docs.text:
For a relay FPGA, instantiate a secondary endpoint toward upstream and primary endpoints toward downstream. Share the synchronized local HeartBeatUnit time base with the downstream primary endpoints: use its heartbeatOut for their syncPulseIn, and pass the upstream secondary endpoint's accumulated fineOffset to each downstream primary endpoint's upstreamOffset. Hold the downstream-facing main blocks in reset until the upstream time solution is ready, while allowing their MIKUMARI clocks and links to operate. The RTL has no separate validity input for upstreamOffset.

Forward the HBU frame information through the LACCP interconnects. For an upstream endpoint A and downstream endpoint B using interconnect index 0, the basic same-clock connections are:

-- A and B denote signal prefixes for two LaccpMainBlock instances.
b_inter_data_in(0)  <= a_inter_data_out(0);
b_inter_valid_in(0) <= a_inter_valid_out(0);
a_inter_ready_in(0) <= b_exist_inter_out(0);

a_inter_data_in(0)  <= b_inter_data_out(0);
a_inter_valid_in(0) <= b_inter_valid_out(0);
b_inter_ready_in(0) <= a_exist_inter_out(0);

Configure both endpoints with at least one interconnect and use only implemented array elements. existInterOut indicates that a port exists, not that downstream synchronization has completed. The direct wiring above requires a shared clock domain and the supplied FIFO-based receiver behavior; add an explicit clock-domain crossing if the endpoint clocks differ.

The relay's HBU can receive the upstream frame information through the upstream endpoint's external intra port while its interconnects carry that information toward downstream endpoints. An unused local HBU port on a downstream-facing endpoint can be tied inactive. Design the interconnect fan-out according to the bus forwarding rules, and distribute reset and acquisition-readiness decisions consistently across the relay.
